articles.title: Knowing why a position closed in MQL5 with OnTradeTransaction
articles.excerpt: A common question in Expert Advisor code is "did my trade just hit its stop loss, its take profit, or did someone close it by hand?" Many EAs answer it by comparing the list of open positions on every…
articles.body: A common question in Expert Advisor code is "did my trade just hit its stop loss, its take profit, or did someone close it by hand?" Many EAs answer it by comparing the list of open positions on every tick and guessing. That works until two things happen on the same tick, or the EA restarts in the middle. MQL5 gives you a better tool: OnTradeTransaction . The terminal calls it for every change on the account, and once a deal is added to history you can read exactly why it happened. The event you care about A trade request produces several transactions: the order is added, updated, removed, a deal is added, the position changes. For "why did this position close", the one to watch is TRADE_TRANSACTION_DEAL_ADD . A deal is the actual execution, and it carries a reason code.

articles.title: Solana’s 150ms Finality Upgrade: What It Means for RPC Infrastructure
articles.excerpt: From 12.8 seconds to approximately 150 milliseconds: How Alpenglow is reshaping transaction finality, data streaming, and blockchain infrastructure. Solana has completed one of the most significant ch…
articles.body: From 12.8 seconds to approximately 150 milliseconds: How Alpenglow is reshaping transaction finality, data streaming, and blockchain infrastructure. Solana has completed one of the most significant changes to its consensus architecture. With the Alpenglow upgrade activated on mainnet on October 21, 2026, the network aims to reduce transaction finality from approximately 12.8 seconds to just 150 milliseconds, representing a reduction of nearly 99%. For users, this could mean faster settlement and more responsive blockchain applications. For developers and infrastructure providers, the implications go considerably deeper. Faster finality changes how applications confirm transactions, consume blockchain data, and manage real-time operations.

articles.excerpt: NASA Science wants to deliver science faster, so we’re changing how we compete and select missions. On Monday, October 26, we will host a virtual NASA Science Town Hall.
articles.body: Dear NASA Science Community, NASA Science wants to deliver science faster, so we’re changing how we compete and select missions. On Monday, October 26, we will host a virtual NASA Science Town Hall, from NASA Headquarters, to explain our new Competition Model 2.0 (CM 2.0), and answer your questions. We have heard you. We have listened. We know that the burden of bringing great ideas forward has been too heavy for too long. It has taken years to move mission concepts through the current two-step process. articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 21, 2008: India launches its 1st mission to the moon with Chandrayaan-1
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor. Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. (Launch occurred at 8:52 p.m. EDT, though it was about 6:22 a.m. local time at the launch site on Oct. 22.) It arrived in lunar orbit about three weeks later and dropped off the Moon Impact Probe, which crashed into the moon on Nov. 14. The rest of the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft stayed in orbit, where it collected and transmitted data from the moon to Earth for about a year.
